notizie.titolo: US attorneys are freeing children from Trump’s ‘deportation machine’ with a new strategy
notizie.riassunto: Exclusive: Immigration advocates are securing early release of minors by filing habeas corpus petitions amid crackdown Migrant children stranded alone in prolonged Trump administration custody and targeted by whole-of-government efforts to deport them are starting to win release while they fight their cases – with a fresh legal strategy, the Guardian has found.

notizie.titolo: ‘Progress takes time’: Stonewall CEO on turning down the heat on the trans debate
notizie.riassunto: Leader is charting a course through troubled waters as a new survey finds trans people feel more pessimistic about social acceptance after combative decade Transgender people fear social acceptance is going into reverse and some are retreating from public spaces, according to the first major analysis since last year’s supreme court ruling in the UK on the definition of a woman.

notizie.titolo: UK police should not have let US force take over airbase trial, MoD documents show
notizie.riassunto: According to documents obtained by the Guardian, officials accused Cambridgeshire force of breaching US-UK deal by handing over case of woman strangled by US pilot Ministry of Defence officials have privately accused a UK police force of wrongly handing over the investigation of an American fighter pilot who strangled a British woman to the US military, according to documents obtained by the Guardian.

notizie.titolo: Trump boosted half of US coal plants with taxpayer dollars and ‘free passes to pollute’, report says
notizie.riassunto: Environmental Defense Fund analysis shows administration handed out $950m and Clean Air Act exemptions It’s a good time to be a coal plant in the US. The Trump administration has given support to almost half of the nation’s coal plants, helping them to continue operating despite economic and regulatory headwinds, according to a new analysis by the Environmental Defense Fund.

notizie.riassunto: UK chancellor’s plans add to concerns government is moving away from pro-renewables agenda John Healey has said he will veto new offshore wind projects if they will not lower bills, adding to concerns that the government is moving away from the pro-renewables agenda.

notizie.titolo: Charges dropped against man arrested in mass shooting at Ohio festival that wounded 12
notizie.riassunto: Eljay Crisp-Carr, 20, spent five months behind bars before prosecutors asked to dismiss charges Ohio prosecutors on Friday dropped charges against a man arrested in connection with the 6 June shooting at Toledo’s Old West End festival that injured 12 people. Eljay Crisp-Carr, 20, had faced more than 50 felony charges stemming from the shooting, including 25 counts of attempted murder.

notizie.titolo: The Iran war is deepening the US energy crisis. A bad winter is ahead | Mark Wolfe
notizie.riassunto: Congress must act to ensure that families are able to heat their homes before the start of the season Heating oil may be the clearest warning yet of how the war in Iran is deepening the US’s energy affordability crisis. Families who heat their homes with oil are facing bills that could be 50% higher this winter, adding nearly $900 to the cost of keeping their homes warm.

notizie.titolo: Public sector an ‘afterthought’ to North Sea oil jobs, says Unison leader
notizie.riassunto: Andrea Egan calls for same political focus on teachers, care sector and NHS and says Jackdaw decision ‘a serious misstep’ The leader of the UK’s biggest trade union has called for the same political focus to be given to NHS, education and care sector workers as there has been on those employed in North Sea oil and gas.

notizie.riassunto: Expressions of disappointment are not an adequate response to the concerning lack of safety improvements for children on social media One thing is clear following last week’s report from the media regulator, Ofcom: the mammoth task of protecting children from online harms has barely begun.

notizie.riassunto: Survivors tell rights group that serving officers who worked as guards administered electric shocks and beatings Cambodian police and military officers worked as private security guards in scam compounds where thousands were forced to work in the online fraud industry, according to a report by Amnesty International.

notizie.titolo: Rosebank oilfield would not breach UK emission targets, say government insiders
